facts.statement: The genus Arandaspis was described by Ritchie and Gilbert-Tomlinson in 1977.
Fossils of Arandaspis were discovered in the Stairway Sandstone near Alice Springs, Australia, in 1959.
facts.quote: Its remains were found in the Stairway Sandstone near Alice Springs, Australia in 1959

facts.statement: Arandaspis represents one of the earliest records of an Ordovician vertebrate from the southern hemisphere.
facts.quote: The discovery of Arandaspis makes it one of the first record of a Ordovician vertebrate from the southern hemisphere.

facts.statement: The name Arandaspis honors the local Indigenous Australian people known as the Aranda, now called the Arrernte.
facts.quote: Arandaspis is named after a local Indigenous Australian people, the Aranda (now currently called Arrernte).

facts.statement: Arandaspis is estimated to have reached a length of 12 to 14 centimeters.
facts.quote: Arandaspis is estimated to reach around 12-14 cm long.

facts.statement: The body of Arandaspis was covered in rows of knobbly armored scutes.
facts.quote: It has a body covered in rows of knobbly armoured scutes.

facts.statement: Comparisons with other early ostracoderms suggest that Arandaspis lacked paired fins.
facts.quote: According to comparisons with other early ostracoderms, it would have lacked paired fins

facts.statement: Arandaspis lived during the Early Ordovician, approximately 480 to 470 million years ago.
facts.quote: Arandaspis es un género extinto de peces agnatos (sin mandíbulas) que vivieron en el Ordovícico Inferior, hace unos 480-470 millones de años.

facts.statement: Arandaspis is considered one of the oldest known vertebrates.
facts.quote: Es uno de los vertebrados más antiguos que se conocen.

facts.statement: Arandaspis measured approximately 15 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Arandaspis medía unos 15 cm de longitud

facts.statement: Although it lacked jaws, Arandaspis may have had movable mouth plates used like lips to suck up food particles.
facts.quote: Aunque no tenía mandíbulas, Arandaspis pudo tener algunas placas móviles en la boca que pudo utilizar como labios para succionar las partículas de las que se alimentaba

facts.statement: The low position of the mouth suggests that Arandaspis fed on the sea floor.
facts.quote: la posición baja de la boca sugiere que se alimentaba sobre el fondo del mar.

facts.statement: Arandaspis lacked fins and relied on a horizontally flattened tail for propulsion.
facts.quote: Carecía de aletas y su único método de propulsión sería la cola, aplanada horizontalmente

facts.statement: Arandaspis lived from the Floian to the Darriwilian stages, between 477.1 and 458.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Floian to Darriwilian (477.1 to 458.2 million years ago)
